editorial.headline: Plastic and Bioplastic Packaging, Open Nationally and Clear for Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 22202 covers the making of plastic and bioplastic packaging, with access across all business scales and no Bali moratorium block in the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 22202 is a manufacturing code for packaging made from plastic and bioplastic. Its scope is practical and broad: bags and plastic pouches, sacks, cosmetic packaging, film packaging, medicine packaging, food packaging, and other plastic packaging forms such as containers, bottles, boxes, cases, racks, and similar items. In plain English, this is the industrial home for businesses that turn plastic or bioplastic into packaging products, whether the final format is flexible, rigid, consumer-facing, or part of a product supply chain.

The record opens the activity to every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because this is not framed only as a large-factory category. A small packaging producer and a larger industrial operation both sit inside the same activity description, provided the business is actually making the packaging products described in the scope. The code is therefore less about a single product shape and more about the function of the output: packaging made from plastic or bioplastic, including packaging for food, cosmetics, medicines, film, and general storage or presentation.

Nationally, the foreign-investment picture is straightforward. The activity is marked TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing at 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That means the national record treats this activity as open to foreign ownership up to the stated ceiling. There is no basis in the slim record to add a separate capital threshold, special licence, local partnership condition, or narrower operational test. The clean reading is that a foreign-owned setup may use this code nationally, up to the 100% foreign-ownership ceiling shown in the record.

Bali does not add a separate percentage in this record. The Bali-side status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason is specific: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium". The moratorium rule in the record says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent, but this activity is not marked as blocked. So the honest national-vs-Bali picture is aligned rather than contradictory: nationally foreign-open, and in Bali not blocked by the moratorium according to the fields provided. The practical conclusion is narrow but useful: for this record, KBLI 22202 can be read as a plastic and bioplastic packaging manufacturing activity that remains available across all listed scales, with a 100% national foreign-ownership ceiling and no Bali moratorium block recorded.
editorial.pullQuote: For this record, the national foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, and Bali is not marked as blocked by the moratorium.
